readonly.py:338-355. For backtick, line 345 skips the 2-char escape jump, so a backslash is plain data and only a doubled backtick (349-351) continues the identifier. A backslash directly before the active quote is refused (342-344) for all three quote characters, so a scanner boundary can differ from MySQL's only on input that is rejected. Elsewhere the boundaries agree in default, NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES and ANSI_QUOTES modes. For `'a\\'`, the pair \\ is skipped and the next quote closes, which is where MySQL closes in both escape modes. `SELECT `a\` FROM t` is refused conservatively (a false positive), not mis-scanned. Wording about the 'only a doubled backtick' rule is slightly looser than the refusal, but the boundary-alignment property holds.

readonly.py:366-369: after '--', following = sql[i+2:i+3]; if non-empty and not (ord<=32 or ==127) it raises UnsafeSqlError; empty following (end of string) falls through to the comment handling at 370-380. This matches MySQL's documented rule (-- needs whitespace or control character after it; the lexer treats the NUL/end after -- as a control char, so SELECT 1-- is a comment). Non-ASCII such as U+00A0 is rejected, which is conservative (fail-closed). I did not run sqlglot or MySQL; this rests on reading the code and MySQL's documented lexer behavior.

_mysql_parse_sql (readonly.py:327-382) scans before sqlglot.parse (line 396, only for mysql/None dialect). Quoted strings/identifiers are skipped as units (338-355) so `/*!` inside them is not falsely rejected and they are copied unchanged; an unterminated quote consumes the rest, which is a string in MySQL too, so no executable comment can hide. `/*!` and `/*M!` are rejected at 357-358 whenever seen outside quotes/comments; `/*` inside other comments is rejected as nested (362), and `/*!` inside -- or # line comments is a real comment in MySQL. Lowercase `/*m!` is not a MariaDB executable-comment opener. CR normalization (376-378) only touches comment text, never literals or identifiers. Tried input: `'a' /*!50000 DROP*/` is rejected; `select '/*!x*/'` is preserved.

Traced _mysql_parse_sql (readonly.py:327-382), used for dialect mysql or None (line 395). Double dash followed by a non-whitespace/control char raises (366-369); '/*' inside a block comment raises (362-363); backslash followed by the active quote raises in all quote types (342-344), independent of NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES. Other backslashes are skipped as data (345-347), and quoted comment markers are skipped by the quote loop (338-355). Standard comments are skipped. CR replacement (376-378) runs only over indices i..end of a '#' or '--' line comment, which is only reached outside quotes; literals, identifiers and block comments are untouched. Hostile input tried: a CR plus a quote inside a '-- ' comment is blanked only in comment text, and a backslash-escaped backtick in an identifier is refused. No counterexample found.

release-notes.md:13 gives migration guidance only for backslash-escaped quotes and adjacent minus signs. _mysql_parse_sql (readonly.py:356-365) also newly refuses a nested '/*' inside a block comment (line 362-363) and an unterminated '/*' comment (360-361); the note's wording ('ambiguous MySQL quote/comment boundaries') names the category but gives no remediation for these. Also '--' followed by any non-whitespace character (366-369, e.g. '--x', '--(') is rejected, while the guidance mentions only minus signs. The claim that the guidance is complete is therefore false for nested/unterminated comments. Ordinary reads and SHOW subkinds remain supported (lines 410-422).

MySQL treats `--` as a comment only when followed by whitespace or a control character, so `SELECT 1--1 AS n` is 1 - (-1) = 2. The test at tests/integration/test_connectors.py:134-138 reads `result.iloc[0]["n"]`, the same DataFrame access pattern the existing test_select_one uses at lines 146-148 (`df.shape`, `df.iloc[0]["n"]`). The column label is the alias `n`, which MySQL does not upper-case. I did not read the vanna MySQL runner itself, because it is outside the repo view (src/sqllens/agent/factory.py has no frame-construction code). The DataFrame return type therefore rests on the sibling test's usage.
